title: Disabling the Sensitivity Settings for DLP Engines

blocks.text: Data sensitivity determines how susceptible the data is along with the level of risk associated with it, which could lead to data breaches. For example, the sensitivity level is high for personally identifiable information (PII) or credit card numbers, moderate for email addresses, and low for data that does not have any sensitive or confidential information.

AI Security scans the data using the predefined DLP engines and dictionaries to detect and classify sensitive data and generates issues. By default, the sensitivity setting is enabled for all DLP engines. You can disable the sensitivity setting when you don't want the DLP engines to classify the data as sensitive.

If you disable the sensitivity setting for all DLP engines, any new DLP engine that is added to Internet & SaaS (ZIA) is not automatically synced with AI Security. You need to manually enable the sensitivity settings for such DLP engines in the AI Security Admin Portal.

blocks.item: On the Data Classification page, disable the sensitivity setting for all DLP engines.
Read the confirmation message that appears, then click Disable.
Disable the data sensitivity setting for a specific DLP engine.
Read the confirmation message that appears, then click Disable.
